hypothesis: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) models, which combine parametric and non-parametric memory components for knowledge-intensive tasks, could be adapted to enhance de novo molecular design by integrating extensive chemical knowledge from external databases. This approach could improve the generation of novel drug-like molecules by providing more factual, specific, and diverse outputs, similar to how RAG models outperform traditional methods in generating responses for knowledge-intensive tasks [2005.11401:1]. By leveraging RAG's ability to access and utilize vast external knowledge, de novo design processes could become more efficient, potentially reducing the time and cost associated with traditional drug discovery methods [denovo-genai-survey:1].
